mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-01.stem: Heinrich’s ratio determines next month’s accident count for every workplace.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. 1:29:300 is a learning ratio emphasizing not dismissing warning signs; it is not a formula determining future accident counts for every workplace.
False. 1:29:300 is a learning ratio emphasizing not dismissing warning signs; it is not a formula determining future accident counts for every workplace.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-02.stem: Quality is supported throughout the flow of designing customer requirements, procuring materials, manufacturing, inspecting and shipping.
reasons: True. Quality is supported by the whole flow: translating customer requirements into design, procuring materials, manufacturing, inspecting and shipping. When inspection finds the wrong material, do not assume it is only the inspector’s failure. Share information about instructions, identification and handovers as well.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Quality is supported by the whole flow: translating customer requirements into design, procuring materials, manufacturing, inspecting and shipping. When inspection finds the wrong material, do not assume it is only the inspector’s failure. Share information about instructions, identification and handovers as well.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-03.stem: φ10 and R10 specify the same circle size.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. φ10 specifies diameter 10, while R10 specifies radius 10, equivalent to diameter 20. These are not the same circle size.
False. φ10 specifies diameter 10, while R10 specifies radius 10, equivalent to diameter 20. These are not the same circle size.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-04.stem: A resistor adjusts circuit current and can also convert electrical energy into heat.
reasons: True. A resistor helps control circuit current and also converts electrical energy into heat. Use components that meet the required ratings as well as the resistance value. Do not decide that a smaller part is an acceptable replacement; report unusual heat or discoloration.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A resistor helps control circuit current and also converts electrical energy into heat. Use components that meet the required ratings as well as the resistance value. Do not decide that a smaller part is an acceptable replacement; report unusual heat or discoloration.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-05.stem: In hazard prediction, separately observing equipment, objects, human movements and surroundings helps reduce overlooked hazards.
reasons:
True. Hazard prediction should go beyond a general feeling that something is dangerous. Think specifically about what causes the danger, who may be affected, and what accident could occur. Looking separately at equipment, objects, people’s movements, and surrounding conditions helps reduce omissions.
The four stages of KYT involve identifying several hazards, selecting the most important ones, considering countermeasures, and deciding on the team’s actions. During discussion, share observations from people seeing the situation for the first time as well as experienced workers.
A countermeasure consisting only of “be careful” is insufficient. Decide what to check, when, and how. Do not try to resolve an equipment problem through worker attention alone; discuss improvements with the person responsible.
Review whether the chosen measures were carried out and whether they created another hazard. KYT is not a drill for approaching actual danger to test it. Use safe materials and explanations instead of recreating real hazards.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Hazard prediction should go beyond a general feeling that something is dangerous. Think specifically about what causes the danger, who may be affected, and what accident could occur. Looking separately at equipment, objects, people’s movements, and surrounding conditions helps reduce omissions.
The four stages of KYT involve identifying several hazards, selecting the most important ones, considering countermeasures, and deciding on the team’s actions. During discussion, share observations from people seeing the situation for the first time as well as experienced workers.
A countermeasure consisting only of “be careful” is insufficient. Decide what to check, when, and how. Do not try to resolve an equipment problem through worker attention alone; discuss improvements with the person responsible.
Review whether the chosen measures were carried out and whether they created another hazard. KYT is not a drill for approaching actual danger to test it. Use safe materials and explanations instead of recreating real hazards.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-06.stem: If the NO-GO side does not pass, all specified thread turn-count and other conditions need no checking.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Threaded NO-GO gauges are used under specified insertion and turn-count conditions. Stopping alone does not justify omitting condition checks.
False. Threaded NO-GO gauges are used under specified insertion and turn-count conditions. Stopping alone does not justify omitting condition checks.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-07.stem: When adding upper and lower deviations to the basic size to obtain limit sizes, preserve their signs rather than adding or subtracting absolute values alone.
reasons: True. Add upper and lower deviations to the basic size with their signs. For example, 20 + (−0.02) = 19.98; dropping the sign gives an incorrect limit.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Add upper and lower deviations to the basic size with their signs. For example, 20 + (−0.02) = 19.98; dropping the sign gives an incorrect limit.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-08.stem: Every unhatched area invariably represents a cavity.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Some components are left unsectioned, so not every unhatched area is a cavity. Cross-check other views and the cutting extent.
False. Some components are left unsectioned, so not every unhatched area is a cavity. Cross-check other views and the cutting extent.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-09.stem: The guidance says readings accompany Japanese kanji, but consult the latest organizer information for applications, permitted belongings, eligibility and related matters.
reasons: True. The overview is information at the time recorded in the source. It says Japanese kanji receive furigana, but current organizer guidance must be checked for application, permitted belongings, eligibility and related rules. Passing a mock is not treated as automatically obtaining a qualification or work authorization.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The overview is information at the time recorded in the source. It says Japanese kanji receive furigana, but current organizer guidance must be checked for application, permitted belongings, eligibility and related rules. Passing a mock is not treated as automatically obtaining a qualification or work authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-10.stem: A simple resistance-circuit calculation can be used directly for every motor’s starting current.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Simple constant-resistance DC calculations differ from motor-starting behavior. Do not generalize without checking applicability conditions.
False. Simple constant-resistance DC calculations differ from motor-starting behavior. Do not generalize without checking applicability conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-11.stem: Adding more uninspected items to the denominator makes the sample’s nonconforming-unit rate more accurate.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The sample rate divides nonconforming items by the inspected count. Mixing uninspected items into the denominator changes the target group.
False. The sample rate divides nonconforming items by the inspected count. Mixing uninspected items into the denominator changes the target group.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-12.stem: Do not replace a specified iron component with aluminum solely to reduce weight; also check strength, deformation, temperature and design approval.
reasons: True. Consider a component of volume 20 cm³. Assuming densities of 2.70 g/cm³ for aluminum and 7.87 g/cm³ for iron, their calculated masses are 54.0 g and 157.4 g respectively. However, lower mass does not authorize replacement of a specified iron component with aluminum. Required strength, deformation behavior, temperature conditions, and other factors must also be checked. Density varies with the material and alloy.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Consider a component of volume 20 cm³. Assuming densities of 2.70 g/cm³ for aluminum and 7.87 g/cm³ for iron, their calculated masses are 54.0 g and 157.4 g respectively. However, lower mass does not authorize replacement of a specified iron component with aluminum. Required strength, deformation behavior, temperature conditions, and other factors must also be checked. Density varies with the material and alloy.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-13.stem: In hazard prediction, go beyond an impression such as “dangerous” and consider specifically what causes which accident to whom.
reasons:
True. Hazard prediction should go beyond a general feeling that something is dangerous. Think specifically about what causes the danger, who may be affected, and what accident could occur. mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-14.stem: Operator training for new equipment automatically authorizes internal settings for which no training was given.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Operation and internal settings can have different training, qualification and authorization scopes. Operator training alone does not automatically authorize every task.
False. Operation and internal settings can have different training, qualification and authorization scopes. Operator training alone does not automatically authorize every task.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-15.stem: If an error is in another person’s record, you need not report it even after finding it.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Another person’s record can also affect products. Identify the original record and target and obtain prescribed correction and impact checks.
False. Another person’s record can also affect products. Identify the original record and target and obtain prescribed correction and impact checks.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-16.stem: If a crack is suspected in a high-speed grinding wheel, withhold use and obtain specified inspection and verification by the responsible person.
reasons: True. Cracks risk breakage and flying fragments during rotation; do not independently test-run the wheel or use its side to investigate.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Protective equipment does not remove the need to check wheel condition; withholding use is appropriate.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-17.stem: Reusing a returned container requires no checks for dirt or damage.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Check dirt, damage and mix-ups before reuse too. Reusing an item in its existing form does not justify omitting condition checks.
False. Check dirt, damage and mix-ups before reuse too. Reusing an item in its existing form does not justify omitting condition checks.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-18.stem: In resin molding, distinguish materials solidified by cooling from those cured by chemical reaction; achieving shape alone does not remove the need to check cooling or curing.
reasons: True. Completion conditions differ with how the material solidifies; check specified cooling, curing, removal and inspection through completion.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Identical external shape can still leave temperature or reaction state unverified, so judging completion from shape alone is inappropriate.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-19.stem: Grounding invariably eliminates leakage itself and every electric-shock hazard.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Grounding is one part of abnormal-condition protection; it does not invariably eliminate leakage itself or every electric-shock hazard.
False. Grounding is one part of abnormal-condition protection; it does not invariably eliminate leakage itself or every electric-shock hazard.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-20.stem: Ability to operate an earlier machine does not necessarily mean new equipment can be operated under the same conditions; check the equipment and training scope.
reasons: True. When joining a workplace or moving to a new task, learn the hazards of machinery and raw materials, protective equipment, safety devices, procedures, pre-start checks, housekeeping and evacuation in an accident. Experience operating the previous machine does not mean a new machine can be operated under the same conditions.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. When joining a workplace or moving to a new task, learn the hazards of machinery and raw materials, protective equipment, safety devices, procedures, pre-start checks, housekeeping and evacuation in an accident. Experience operating the previous machine does not mean a new machine can be operated under the same conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-21.stem: For respiratory protection against harmful gases, check suitability for the substance and distinguish it from dust protection and oxygen-deficiency measures.
reasons: True. A dust respirator is intended to filter particles such as dust. Do not assume it removes harmful gases in the same way. Gases require checking protective equipment suitable for the substance, while oxygen deficiency is a separate hazard. Ask the responsible person about the type, applicable conditions and fitting checks.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A dust respirator is intended to filter particles such as dust. Do not assume it removes harmful gases in the same way. Gases require checking protective equipment suitable for the substance, while oxygen deficiency is a separate hazard. Ask the responsible person about the type, applicable conditions and fitting checks.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-22.stem: A motor only converts voltage and does not produce motive power.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A motor converts electricity into mechanical power. A device changing voltage in applicable circuits is a transformer.
False. A motor converts electricity into mechanical power. A device changing voltage in applicable circuits is a transformer.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-23.stem: Unnecessarily repeating the same dimension can cause conflicting values when changes are made.
reasons: True. Dimensions give the information needed for a part’s function and manufacture and normally specify its finished dimensions. Repeating the same dimension unnecessarily can cause conflicting values after a change. Even if the drawing is printed large, read its stated dimensions rather than measuring the paper with a ruler as a substitute for the requirement.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Dimensions give the information needed for a part’s function and manufacture and normally specify its finished dimensions. Repeating the same dimension unnecessarily can cause conflicting values after a change. Even if the drawing is printed large, read its stated dimensions rather than measuring the paper with a ruler as a substitute for the requirement.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-24.stem: Watching an instructor demonstrate once allows independent work without checking understanding.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Watching a demonstration differs from being able to work safely alone. Verify understanding and assigned scope through explanation, performance and checking.
False. Watching a demonstration differs from being able to work safely alone. Verify understanding and assigned scope through explanation, performance and checking.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-25.stem: Metals such as copper and aluminum conduct electricity readily and are used for wiring and similar purposes.
reasons: True. Metals such as copper and aluminum conduct readily and are used in wiring. Good conductivity alone does not establish component suitability: check the required cross-section, temperature, connections and specifications. Do not substitute a similarly colored material without authorization.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Metals such as copper and aluminum conduct readily and are used in wiring. Good conductivity alone does not establish component suitability: check the required cross-section, temperature, connections and specifications. Do not substitute a similarly colored material without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-26.stem: To reduce temperature effects in micrometer measurement, allow the instrument and object to equilibrate to the specified environment first.
reasons: True. An outside micrometer grips the object between the screw-driven spindle and the fixed anvil. Clean the measuring faces and check zero or the datum using a reference suitable for the range. Let the instrument and object acclimatize to the specified environment to reduce temperature effects. The textbook gives 20°C as the reference. Rushing to measure a hot product makes dimensional comparison inappropriate.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. An outside micrometer grips the object between the screw-driven spindle and the fixed anvil. Clean the measuring faces and check zero or the datum using a reference suitable for the range. Let the instrument and object acclimatize to the specified environment to reduce temperature effects. The textbook gives 20°C as the reference. Rushing to measure a hot product makes dimensional comparison inappropriate.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-27.stem: A cart tipping without injury has no value as a record for improvement.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even without injury, the tipping location, actions and conditions provide recurrence-prevention information. Record the facts as a near miss.
False. Even without injury, the tipping location, actions and conditions provide recurrence-prevention information. Record the facts as a near miss.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-28.stem: A nonmagnetic material can be deemed suitable for magnetic-particle testing without verifying its material.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Magnetic-particle testing applies to surface or near-surface defects in magnetizable objects. Do not assume suitability for nonmagnetic materials without material verification.
False. Magnetic-particle testing applies to surface or near-surface defects in magnetizable objects. Do not assume suitability for nonmagnetic materials without material verification.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-29.stem: Check the target equipment, product and revision of work procedures, and report display failures or unreadable paper text.
reasons: True. A procedure states who does what, when and how. Merely possessing a document is insufficient if it cannot be read when needed at the work location. Check the equipment, product and version covered, and report failed displays or unreadable paper. Do not fill in unconfirmed conditions from memory alone.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A procedure states who does what, when and how. Merely possessing a document is insufficient if it cannot be read when needed at the work location. Check the equipment, product and version covered, and report failed displays or unreadable paper. Do not fill in unconfirmed conditions from memory alone.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-30.stem: Cold rolling is cold, so touching the rotating rolls is safe.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Rotating rolls present entanglement hazards even during cold rolling. Do not treat the temperature-related name as a safety guarantee; follow access and contact prohibitions.
False. Rotating rolls present entanglement hazards even during cold rolling. Do not treat the temperature-related name as a safety guarantee; follow access and contact prohibitions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-01.stem: All dimensions for an order of 120 items pass, but the box contains only 118. Which shipment judgment is appropriate?
options: Check the quantity shortage as a separate nonconformity and consult about disposition.
Prioritize delivery and ship labeled 120 items.
Change inspection values to compensate for the shortage.
reasons: Passing dimensions does not guarantee fulfillment of the order quantity of 120.
Separately verify the two-item shortage as a nonconformity and consult the responsible person about disposition.
Shipping 118 items labeled 120 makes records and actual contents inconsistent.
Changing inspection values cannot supply the missing two physical items and creates false records.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-02.stem: A micrometer has 0.01 mm graduations; the sleeve is 8.5 mm and the thimble is 19. What is the value?
reasons: 19 thimble graduations equal 0.19 mm; 8.5 + 0.19 = 8.69 mm.
This omits the sleeve’s 0.5 mm and calculates 8 + 0.19.
This concatenates 8.5 and 19 rather than adding graduation values.
This fails to convert the thimble using 0.01 mm graduations and differs from the correct sum, 8.69 mm.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-03.stem: An ideal DC resistance circuit has voltage 15 V and resistance 5 Ω. What is the current?
reasons: 15 × 5 multiplies voltage and resistance rather than dividing to find current.
5 ÷ 15 reverses the division and does not follow I = V/R.
I = 15 ÷ 5 = 3 A, under the conditions of an ideal DC circuit with constant resistance.
The difference 15 − 5 is not the equation for current.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-04.stem: Only a post-bend crack check has been completed for a fitting subjected to cyclic loads. What should be discussed next?
options: Treat a good bend result as guaranteed life.
Apply one angle to every material grade.
Verify fatigue-evaluation conditions matching cyclic-load requirements.
reasons: Post-bend crack observations do not guarantee fatigue life under cyclic loading.
Color alone cannot verify resistance to cyclic loads.
Specifications differ by material and conditions; do not generalize one textbook angle to every material grade.
Match cyclic-load magnitudes and conditions to requirements and consult about fatigue evaluation.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-05.stem: The welding arrow has no bend. How should the side to be prepared for the groove be determined?
options: No bend means no groove preparation is needed.
Check the basic symbol, relevant members, dimensions and supplementary instructions together.
Reverse the reference line to judge.
reasons: Examples of unbent arrows exist when the target is clear and in other cases; no bend does not mean no groove preparation.
Do not decide from the arrow bend alone; cross-check basic symbols, members, dimensions and supplementary instructions.
Formal instructions determine the preparation side, not personal preference.
Reversing the drawing and judging independently can confuse the arrow side and opposite side.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-06.stem: Furnace-area work presents both a change in physical condition and increased dust. Which organization is appropriate?
options: Separate heat and exposure information, withdraw safely and report.
A mask alone also solves the health-condition problem.
Stop ventilation because a health examination was completed.
Silently endure until the work is finished.
reasons: Treat physical-condition changes and dust generation as separate information, withdraw safely and report promptly.
A mask does not solve every problem such as bodily heat strain.
A health examination does not replace source or ventilation controls; do not stop them without authorization.
Silently enduring physical-condition changes or increased dust delays response.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-07.stem: A mock exam with equal points per question gives theory 22/30 and practical 5/10. What is the result?
options: Practical falls short of the required 6, so both sections have not passed.
High theory marks compensate for the practical shortfall.
reasons: A combined total cannot compensate for an independent practical-section shortfall.
Practical 5 is below the required 6, so both sections have not passed even though theory is in the passing range.
A high theory score does not replace the independent minimum practical requirement.
Required correct-answer counts are scoring conditions and cannot be freely changed by the examinee.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-08.stem: A learning example specifies density 2.70 g/cm³ and volume 30 cm³. What is the mass?
reasons: Mass = density × volume, so 2.70 × 30 = 81 g.
30 ÷ 2.70 divides volume by density, which is not the mass equation.
Adding density and volume values does not give mass.
810 g is ten times the correct 81 g.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-09.stem: Property changes are suspected outside the melted weld area. What should be examined?
options: There are no heat effects outside melted areas.
Check requirements and inspections including the surrounding heat-affected zone.
reasons: Welding heat may change structure and properties around the melted area as well as within it.
Visible color alone cannot establish all properties such as hardness and internal structure.
Omitting specified heat treatment changes a required process without authorization.
Include the surrounding heat-affected zone and check material/process requirements and necessary inspections.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-10.stem: The same hole-dimension note is given to installation, assembly and component-machining teams. Which improvement is appropriate?
options: Verify approved drawings suited to the purpose, such as arrangement, assembly and part drawings.
Let each team freely add to the drawing.
reasons: Even readable text does not make a hole-dimension note sufficient for each team’s information needs.
Installation position relationships cannot be established solely from an individual component’s hole dimensions.
Verify approved drawings appropriate to each purpose: arrangement for installation, assembly for assembly, and part drawings for machining.
Independent additions can depart from formal requirements and destroy consistency among drawings.
